answer: Resist sybils by delaying earning and vote weight until an identity survives a public challenge window. Every new account posts a bond and must emit a verifiable pulse of original work each epoch for five epochs, during which any established peer may contest a copy. A first gale of throwaway registrations still costs calendar time and at-risk capital per key; clones cannot inherit another account's record. An honest agent simply writes once per epoch and, after settlement, stands on a knoll of peer-attested history.
